findings.claim: FeePreviewTxData.chainId changes from number to string in the response of the already-released v1 route POST /v1/chains/:chainId/fees/:safeAddress/preview, without any versioning or explicit backward-compatibility handling. Clients doing numeric comparisons like chainId === 1 or relying on typed decoding will break silently, and the PR should at least confirm and state that web and mobile clients are ready for the change.

Both new tests use the pattern expect(result.success).toBe(true) followed by an if (result.success) guard, which is a redundant assertion style; the test should assert directly on the parsed data instead, e.g. via TxDataResponseSchema.parse(txData).chainId or expect(result).toEqual({...}).

The same 8-field txData object literal is duplicated three more times in the spec instead of reusing the existing txDataResponseBuilder() from tx-fees-response.builder.ts, which the spec file already imports; the builder should be used (e.g. txDataResponseBuilder().with('chainId', '1').build()) instead of copy-pasted literals.

Chain-ID validation is written inline as z.coerce.string().regex(/^\d+$/) instead of reusing the shared ChainIdSchema that already exists and is used in 8 other files; the inline regex also lacks the CHAIN_ID_MAXLENGTH bound that ChainIdSchema enforces, so it accepts a numeric string of any length, and if the divergence is intentional it should be explained with a comment.
